title: Independent ideas. Extraordinary finds.
intro: A daily selection of independent games and useful Android apps, with original F7 insights and links to their creators.

entries.name: Veloren
entries.summary: Veloren is a community-built fantasy action RPG with a world made from voxels. Explore mountains, deserts and caves, gather materials, craft equipment and fight creatures with different weapon styles. Towns and dungeons give the journey structure, while multiplayer servers let friends explore together. Its procedural world is still being developed, making this a discovery for players who enjoy following an evolving project.
features: Procedural world with caves and dungeons
Weapon-based combat and equipment crafting
Online and LAN multiplayer
entries.insight: Veloren pairs an inviting visual style with systems that make wandering feel purposeful. For F7, it is a useful example of community development shaping both a game's world and its tools, with room for players to become contributors.

entries.name: LocalSend
entries.developer: Tien Do Nam and LocalSend contributors
entries.summary: Move files and text between nearby phones and computers on the same network. LocalSend keeps the transfer local and does not need an account or an internet connection.
features: Share files and text across Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Find receiving devices over your local Wi-Fi network.
Protect transfers with HTTPS encryption and an optional receiving PIN.
entries.insight: A practical bridge between a phone and a work computer. We like the short path from choosing a file to delivering it, especially when a cloud upload would add an unnecessary step.

entries.name: Unciv
entries.summary: Unciv packages civilization-building strategy into a compact interface for Android and desktop. Develop cities, research technologies, manage an expanding civilization and compete with rival powers. The project emphasizes modding and lightweight presentation, with its own illustrated tiles and icons rather than elaborate animation. It is a free community project aimed at players who want long strategic decisions in a small, practical package.
features: City growth and technology research
Moddable 4X strategy
Android and desktop play
entries.insight: Unciv is a good reminder that strategic depth can come from rules and readable feedback. Its restrained presentation makes it worth studying for small teams building ambitious systems without a large animation or rendering budget.

entries.name: Fossify Gallery
entries.summary: An Android gallery for managing photos and videos stored on your device. Its editing and organisation tools are designed around a local library, with no internet permission required.
features: Browse local photo and video folders and organise albums.
Crop, rotate, resize, draw on, and apply filters to images.
Hide selected folders and recover deleted items through the recycle bin.
entries.insight: Worth a look when the camera roll needs attention. The combination of local browsing, everyday edits, and a recovery bin covers the jobs many people otherwise split across several apps.

entries.name: 0 A.D.
entries.summary: 0 A.D. is a historical real-time strategy game made by Wildfire Games' international volunteer team. Build a city, gather resources and raise an army with a civilization whose units, buildings and technologies shape its play style. Citizen soldiers can work as well as fight, tying economic decisions to military strength. An included map editor and accessible game files also make it a place to explore scenario design and modding.
features: Distinct civilizations and technology trees
Citizen soldiers who build, gather and fight
Atlas map editor and mod support
entries.insight: The citizen-soldier system makes 0 A.D. especially interesting: economic workers and military units are partly the same people. That connection gives small changes in timing a strategic cost, a useful idea for designers exploring economy and combat together.

entries.name: AntennaPod
entries.summary: Build a podcast library from RSS feeds and keep episodes ready for listening away from a connection. AntennaPod pairs a flexible queue with practical controls for a regular listening routine.
features: Subscribe to podcasts using their RSS feeds.
Download episodes for offline listening and configure automatic downloads.
Adjust playback speed and automate deletion of finished episodes.
entries.insight: A good discovery for listeners who want to choose their own feeds. Automatic downloads and cleanup make it especially appealing for a commute or a recurring listening schedule.

entries.name: SuperTuxKart
entries.summary: SuperTuxKart is a colorful arcade racing game built around open-source project mascots. Race through varied tracks, use powerups and tackle a story mode, Grand Prix cups or time trials. Local and online multiplayer support shared competition, while soccer, battle and egg-hunt modes offer different ways to use the same driving skills. Community tracks and karts extend what is included in the main download.
features: Story, Grand Prix and time-trial modes
Local and online multiplayer
Community karts and tracks
entries.insight: SuperTuxKart shows how a familiar control scheme can support very different goals. Its extra modes are worth exploring as examples of reusing a game's strongest mechanics, and its community addons show how a small project can keep expanding.

entries.name: URLCheck
entries.summary: Put an editable preview between tapping a link and opening it. URLCheck exposes the address, offers optional cleanup modules, and lets you choose the app that should receive it.
features: Inspect and edit a URL before handing it to another app.
Remove recognised tracking parameters with the ClearURLs module.
Check HTTP status and follow redirects in deliberate steps.
entries.insight: Small links can hide a lot of routing. This adds a useful pause for understanding where a shared address goes, although a cleaner URL is not a guarantee that a destination is trustworthy.

entries.name: Pioneer
entries.summary: Pioneer is an open-ended space adventure set across a simulated Milky Way. Fly between star systems, land on planets and choose how to earn a living through trade, missions or less lawful work. Its emphasis on flight and a vast galaxy gives journeys as much weight as destinations. The project is still in development, with free Windows and Linux builds available from its official download page.
features: Explore millions of star systems
Planetary landings and spaceflight
Trading, missions and piracy
entries.insight: Pioneer is worth discovering for the sense of scale created by travel rather than a fixed sequence of levels. It offers a useful reference for designers thinking about how movement, distance and player freedom can become the main experience.

entries.name: Material Files
entries.summary: Manage local files and network folders through an Android file browser with clear navigation. Material Files brings archive tools and several server protocols into the same interface.
features: Use breadcrumb navigation to move between folder levels.
View, create, and extract common archive formats.
Access files on FTP, SFTP, SMB, and WebDAV servers.
entries.insight: A useful step up when moving files extends beyond Downloads. We particularly like having archives and a home server within reach of the same folder navigation.

entries.name: Naev
entries.summary: Naev is a top-down space game about finding a place in a galaxy of trade, combat and faction politics. Fly different ships, customize their equipment and earn money through missions or other work. Its real-time movement uses semi-Newtonian physics, while a built-in plugin manager makes community additions easier to explore. This is a continuing hobby project with free downloads for Windows, macOS and Linux.
features: Semi-Newtonian real-time spaceflight
Customizable ships and distinct factions
Built-in plugin manager
entries.insight: Naev puts a lot of variety behind a clear top-down view. The combination of flight feel, ship choices and community plugins is worth exploring for anyone interested in how a focused interface can support a large game.

entries.name: HeliBoard
entries.summary: An Android keyboard with extensive layout and theme controls. HeliBoard works without internet permission and gives multilingual typing, clipboard tools, and alternative keyboard arrangements a central place.
features: Customise keyboard layouts, colours, and themes.
Type in multiple languages and add dictionaries for suggestions.
Use clipboard history, one-handed mode, and split layouts.
entries.insight: A keyboard is one of the most-used tools on a phone. HeliBoard is worth exploring if key placement, language switching, or a particular screen size makes the default keyboard feel awkward.

entries.name: Endless Sky
entries.summary: Endless Sky is a free space trading and combat game where a tiny starter ship is the beginning of an open-ended career. Carry cargo or passengers, accept missions, hunt pirates and use the proceeds to improve your ship or build a fleet. A story campaign runs alongside that freedom, so players can follow its conflicts or spend their time exploring and making their own living.
features: Trading, passenger jobs and missions
Ship upgrades and fleet building
Story campaign with open exploration
entries.insight: The appeal of Endless Sky is the way a small starting ship gives progression a clear meaning. Each upgrade changes what work becomes possible, making it an approachable reference for designers connecting an economy to player freedom.

entries.name: StreetComplete
entries.summary: Turn a walk into small improvements to OpenStreetMap. StreetComplete marks nearby gaps in map data and asks questions you can answer by observing the place in front of you.
features: Find nearby places that need a survey through map quest markers.
Answer plain-language questions without learning OpenStreetMap tags.
Survey offline and upload map edits through your OpenStreetMap account.
entries.insight: An appealing way to contribute something useful during an ordinary walk. The task-sized questions lower the barrier to mapping, while on-site observation keeps each answer grounded in the real place.
